items.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I don't know the biography. I can tell you, when you interview Michael Cuscuna, he knows everything. I only know mine from the experience of it with him.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well I’d like to talk for a moment about Alfred, coming from Germany, in the ‘30s, and whether or not the atmosphere, the social atmosphere that he lived in, do you think it had an effect on him looking for something else, and finding it in American jazz.

I do believe so. Because Alfred had a very structured personality. He was a person who had come up in a very — he was raised in military schools, from a little kid, maybe five or six years of age. So everything — I mean he was meticulous in everything he did. So I think that when he was a kid, he went skating and he heard instead of there being skating that day, there was Sam Wooding, the orchestra, the old time orchestra. This was back in the 20s. So he went and listened to them. And he never got over that, that…
